selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What main lesson is introduced at the beginning of this passage through the comparison?
questions.answer: Human abilities were not given mainly for chasing worldly comfort like animals do.

questions.question: What does the difference between twenty gold pieces and one thousand gold pieces suggest in the comparison?
questions.answer: It suggests that different amounts point to different levels of responsibility and purpose.

questions.question: What was unreasonable about spending the larger sum the same way as the smaller sum?
questions.answer: A much greater amount clearly pointed to a broader purpose, so using it the same way ignored common sense.

questions.question: What conclusion should “anyone with any sense” reach from the two different amounts?
questions.answer: The larger amount was meant for something more than buying clothes.

questions.question: What deeper problem is shown by the second servant’s copying of the first servant?
questions.answer: He acted without reflection and failed to think about his own purpose.

questions.question: Why is the contrast between fine cloth and inferior cloth important?
questions.answer: It highlights how badly he handled a much greater opportunity.

questions.question: What did the second servant buy, and how was its quality described?
questions.answer: He spent everything on clothing and ended up with poor material and a much worse outfit.

questions.question: According to the final warning, how are humans superior to animals?
questions.answer: Humans are superior because they have much greater inner resources and potential.

questions.question: What does the comparison with animals teach about human responsibility?
questions.answer: Since humans have higher capacities, they are responsible for living in a higher way than animals.

questions.question: What makes the fall of a human being worse than that of an animal?
questions.answer: A human falls further because he turns higher gifts toward lower ends.

questions.question: What claim about human faculties does the passage ask the reader to understand?
questions.answer: It asks the reader to see that human powers were not created just for material life.

questions.question: Why is the written paper important in the story?
questions.answer: It shows that the second servant had guidance and a specific duty to understand.

questions.question: Besides receiving more money, how was the second servant’s situation different from the first servant’s?
questions.answer: He was also sent with written directions for a separate business matter.

questions.question: What should the second servant have done before spending the money?
questions.answer: He should have read the note and understood his assignment.

questions.question: How did the second servant fail both intellectually and morally?
questions.answer: He failed to think clearly and also misused what was entrusted to him.

questions.question: How did the second servant decide what to do instead?
questions.answer: He copied the first servant without understanding his own different responsibility.

questions.question: In the direct address to the self and friend, what kind of life is being criticized?
questions.answer: A life focused on bodily desires and short-term worldly pleasures is being criticized.

questions.question: How does the comparison strengthen the warning given at the end?
questions.answer: The story gives a concrete example that makes the moral failure of wasting one’s life easier to understand.

questions.question: What is the consequence of misusing that greater capital?
questions.answer: The consequence is a deeper fall in worth and conduct.

questions.question: How does the passage compare humans and animals at the end, and what is the point of that comparison?
questions.answer: It says humans have far greater capacity than animals, so if they live only for appetite, they can sink even lower than animals despite having more noble gifts.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the story about the two servants?
questions.answer: It is meant to explain how human abilities should be used wisely and for higher aims.

questions.question: What was special about the cloth used by the first servant?
questions.answer: It was of very fine quality.

questions.question: Why is the amount given to the second servant called “capital” in meaning?
questions.answer: Because it is a valuable resource meant to be invested in a purposeful task.

questions.question: What detail proves that the second servant had guidance available to him?
questions.answer: He had a written message placed in his pocket.

title: Warning to the Wicked and the Self Explanation of Misuse Through a Parable and Awakening the Self
